original_query: Based on the waveform analysis, implement a minimal fix for the identified bug.

history_summaries: Round 1/3: Fix assertion `StateG_to_StateE_when_LINEA0` (assertion_error). Root cause: temporal misalignment — `RegNext(stato)` was placed on the consequence side (delaying the state check by one cycle), making the assertion check whether the *previous* state equals StateE instead of the *next* state. Fixed by wrapping the entire implication in `RegNext(...)`, so the antecedent (stato===StateG && LINEA=0) is sampled in the previous cycle and the consequent (stato===StateE) is checked in the current cycle. This matches the FSM comment: "From StateG, when LINEA is false, the next state is unconditionally StateE." Label preserved unchanged. No homologous assertions found — `U_causal_from_StateE` correctly uses `RegNext(stato)` on the consequence because that property checks the *previous* state, not the *next* state.

Round 2/3: Fix assertion `StateG_to_StateE_when_LINEA0` (assertion_error). Root cause: temporal misalignment — `RegNext` wrapped the entire implication `!(antecedent) || consequent`, so the assertion checked whether the implication held in the *previous* cycle. At t=30, antecedent (stato===StateG & LINEA=0) is true but consequent (stato===StateE) is false (stato=StateG), making the implication false; `RegNext(false)` at t=40 causes the CEX. Fixed by moving `RegNext` to wrap *only the antecedent*: `!RegNext(stato === StateG && io.LINEA === false.B) || stato === StateE`. Now at t=40, `RegNext(...)` is true (sampled at t=30), and `stato === StateE` is true, so the assertion passes. This matches the comment: \"if in the previous cycle we were in StateG with LINEA=0, then in THIS cycle stato must be StateE.\" Label preserved unchanged. No homologous assertions found — all other assertions have different structure (U_single_cycle_pulse uses RegNext on U_reg, U_causal_from_StateE correctly uses RegNext(stato) on the consequence side for a different property).
